name: Strike Anywhere
label: Jade Tree
lede: Named after a song by the singer's old band, Strike Anywhere took Richmond's buried history, a stolen notebook and a Weimar-era antifascist logo and made twenty-five years of angry, tuneful hardcore out of it.

eras.title: Named for an Inquisition song
eras.text: When Richmond punk band Inquisition ended, singer Thomas Barnett started over with a band named after one of its songs. Within a year Strike Anywhere had an EP out and a month on the road with As Friends Rust.

years.h: Thomas Barnett forms Strike Anywhere in Richmond, Virginia
years.p: The name came from a song by Barnett's previous band Inquisition. The first lineup of Barnett, Matt Smith, Matt Sherwood, Garth Petrie and Eric Kane lasted eight years.

years.h: Chorus of One EP on Red Leader and No Idea
years.p: Strike Anywhere's debut EP. Bridge 9 founder Chris Wrenn later said he'd been a fan since this record.

years.h: First tour: four weeks across the US with As Friends Rust
years.p: Strike Anywhere and [[As Friends Rust|2f106f2f-5990-4f50-9590-3fa8da941f98]] crossed the country, stopping at Mixed Messages in Minneapolis and the Pheer Festival in College Park, Maryland.

eras.title: Jade Tree and the Richmond history lesson
eras.text: Jade Tree signed Strike Anywhere in early 2001 and producer Brian McTernan made both of its Jade Tree albums at Salad Days in Maryland. The records were about police brutality, globalization and Richmond's secret past, and they sounded like singalongs.

years.h: Strike Anywhere signs to Jade Tree
years.p: The Wilmington, Delaware label signed the band two months before it recorded its debut album. A 7-inch for Fat Wreck's Fat Club series followed that year.

years.h: Change Is a Sound recorded at Salad Days in Baltimore
years.p: [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] produced, engineered and mixed the album at his own studio.

years.h: Change Is a Sound: police brutality, women's rights, Richmond
years.p: Sunset on 32nd is about police brutality and Chalkline about women's rights. The cover photo, shot on the band's first European tour, shows Tony Pence of the punk band Deep Sleep.
years.xp:
Thomas Barnett said the record was built on local experiences and local stories.

The liner notes backed the vegetarian lifestyle, the living wage movement and the fight against corporate globalization.

years.h: Underground Europe 2001: a benefit EP for Genoa
years.p: Scene Police released the Genoa Benefit EP, tied to the protests against the G8 summit in Genoa that summer.

years.h: Strike Anywhere filmed live at the Camden Underworld in London
years.p: The highlight of a five-week European tour with As Friends Rust. Punkervision released the footage on DVD in December 2002.
years.xp:
The tour ran from October 29 to December 5, 2001. The London set came out as Live at Camden Underworld, a split video with As Friends Rust.

Strike Anywhere has always let fans tape its shows for personal, non-commercial use, and works with the Internet Archive to host those recordings.

years.h: Sunset on 32nd, live, for Amadou Diallo
years.p: Strike Anywhere's police-brutality song appeared on 1157 Wheeler Avenue, a memorial compilation for Amadou Diallo, killed by New York police in 1999.

years.h: Thomas Barnett's lyric notebooks are stolen before Exit English
years.p: Just before recording, Barnett's notebooks of lyrics and song ideas were stolen from his car, so the whole band helped write. Then Brian McTernan pushed him hard on vocals.
years.xp: Barnett recalled spending eight hours a day on vocals at Salad Days, with McTernan satisfied by none of it. He called McTernan really hard on the band.

years.h: Exit English: slave revolts and Richmond's secret history
years.p: The second Jade Tree album dug into Richmond's buried past: slave insurrections, women's riots and the Confederate army burning the city. The title points at English colonialism.

years.h: Tony Hawk's Underground and Punk Goes Acoustic
years.p: Refusal went on the 2003 Tony Hawk's Underground game and an acoustic Chalk Line on Fearless Records' Punk Goes Acoustic.

years.h: To Live in Discontent, Jade Tree and Chunksaah
years.p: A live album co-released by Jade Tree and Chunksaah, the Bouncing Souls' label, closing out the band's Jade Tree years.

years.h: Warped Tour, in the Wake Up Screaming documentary
years.p: Strike Anywhere played the 2005 Vans Warped Tour and appears in Wake Up Screaming, the film about it. Question the Answer also landed on Tony Hawk's American Wasteland.

eras.title: Fat Wreck, a new guitarist, the Iron Front
eras.text: Strike Anywhere moved to Fat Wreck Chords, then Bridge 9, still recording with McTernan. Founding guitarist Matt Sherwood left after a show in New Zealand, and the band named its fourth album after the antifascist symbol it had used all along.

years.h: Dead FM on Fat Wreck, recorded on weekends
years.p: Made on a series of weekends over nine months between tours. Sedition, the opener, draws on Thomas Barnett's grandfather's work on the Manhattan Project.
years.xp: Punknews ranked it the No. 4 release of 2006. Barnett said the politics had shifted from events to more sociological ideas about why these things happen.

years.h: Matt Sherwood's last Strike Anywhere show: Auckland, New Zealand
years.p: The founding guitarist left after the Auckland show. Mark Miller took his place.

years.h: Strike Anywhere signs to Bridge 9
years.p: Punknews reported the deal. Founder Chris Wrenn said he'd been a fan since the band's debut EP.

years.h: Iron Front: named for a Weimar antifascist symbol
years.p: The band's logo had long echoed the Three Arrows of the Iron Front, the German antifascist group of the Weimar Republic's last years. The fourth album took the name.

years.h: Touring Iron Front with Propagandhi and Pennywise
years.p: Tours ran through mid-2010 across North America, Europe, Australia and New Zealand with [[Propagandhi|cc546218-cc08-4ae9-9592-ac1596c1470d]], [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]], Crime in Stereo and Four Year Strong.

eras.title: Acoustic, live, and eleven years later
eras.text: Without a new album for a decade, Strike Anywhere released live sets and kept playing. In 2020 it finally came back with new songs.

years.h: Two live albums on Bridge 9, one acoustic
years.p: In Defiance of Empty Times reworked songs acoustically; Live at the Montage Music Hall caught the band plugged in.

years.h: Thomas Barnett says a fifth album is in the works
years.p: In a December 2016 interview Barnett confirmed he was writing a fifth studio album.

years.h: Nightmares of the West: first new music in 11 years
years.p: Seven tracks on Pure Noise Records, Strike Anywhere's first release of new songs since Iron Front.
